signals.name: Microsoft Corp
signals.label: Congress buying + retail momentum spike
signals.detail: Two separate Congress members disclosed large MSFT buys in September 2026: Rep. Josh Gottheimer ($753,005-$1,545,000, traded 8/14, disclosed 9/14 -- one of the largest single congressional stock purchases disclosed this month) and Rep. Gil Cisneros ($15,001-$50,000 via his '150 Main Street Trust', traded 7/17, disclosed 9/4/9/8). Simultaneously, r/wallstreetbets mention volume for MSFT is up sharply week-over-week per ApeWisdom, currently among the most-discussed tickers on the forum. A counterpoint: Rep. Thomas Kean Jr. (R-NJ) sold $15,001-$50,000 of MSFT (traded 8/27, disclosed 9/15) via the Kean Family Partnership the same cycle.
signals.takeaway: A very large-dollar Congressional buy from a Financial Services/AI-subcommittee member landing alongside a sharp retail-attention spike is a rare alignment worth tracking into Microsoft's next earnings print -- though a same-cycle Kean sell shows the signal isn't unanimous.

signals.name: Palantir Technologies
signals.label: Congress + Street bulls vs. Michael Burry shorting
signals.detail: Rep. Gil Cisneros disclosed a fresh PLTR buy ($1,001-$15,000, traded 7/17, disclosed 9/4/9/8), and sell-side commentary has run bullish through September citing a strong one-month rally and heavy call open interest. Against that, Michael Burry's newsletter has been publicly adding to a PLTR short/put position through September, citing 'channel stuffing' concerns.
signals.takeaway: A textbook consensus-vs-contrarian split -- retail/Congress momentum on one side, a well-known bear explicitly deepening a short on the other -- worth watching for a volatility resolution.

signals.name: Broadcom Inc
signals.label: Congress buying + AI-backlog analyst enthusiasm
signals.detail: Rep. Rick Allen disclosed a fresh AVGO buy ($1,001-$15,000, disclosed 9/22) right after Broadcom's Sept 4 Q3 print (revenue +86% YoY, EPS +215% YoY). Sell-side commentary has flagged further upside potential tied to Broadcom's AI order backlog.
signals.takeaway: Congressional buying lines up with a fresh earnings beat and bullish sell-side commentary on AI infrastructure spend -- a momentum confirmation rather than a divergence.

signals.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
signals.label: Congress buying alongside AVGO -- AI supply-chain theme
signals.detail: Rep. Rick Allen bought TSM in the same Sept 22 disclosure as his AVGO purchase, both in the $1,001-$15,000 bracket, amid continued reporting on Broadcom/TSMC AI capacity constraints.
signals.takeaway: A paired buy alongside AVGO suggests a deliberate AI-supply-chain bet rather than a one-off congressional trade.

signals.name: NVIDIA Corp
signals.label: Congress selling + Burry de-risking -- fading momentum signal
signals.detail: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse disclosed an NVDA sale ($15,001-$50,000, traded 8/13, disclosed 9/2). Separately, Michael Burry closed out his December-2026-dated NVDA/PLTR puts in early September (a risk-reduction move, not a bullish reversal) before continuing to voice a bearish AI-trade view later in the month.
signals.takeaway: Not a clean bearish signal -- Burry's move was de-risking, not capitulation -- but combined with a Congressional sale it points to reduced conviction at the margin near record highs.

signals.name: Micron Technology
signals.label: Retail momentum + multi-member Congress exposure vs. Burry short
signals.detail: MU is among the most-mentioned tickers on r/wallstreetbets this week. Multiple Congress members hold or have recently traded MU, while Michael Burry has been publicly expanding a short position in Micron through September, citing rising memory-supply risk.
signals.takeaway: Retail enthusiasm and standing Congressional exposure are running into an explicit, escalating short thesis from a well-known bear -- a name with genuine two-sided conviction right now.
